Subject: Privacy annex: provisioning process & evidence portal integration

Hi Tom / HealthGrid procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. As follow-up, we scoped the minimal provisioning steps HealthGrid needs to complete to consume evidence for the privacy annex and DPA addendum. Attached is a short provisioning checklist and our evidence spec (redwood-privacy-evidence-spec.pdf). Key asks:

- Admins in your org who should have read access to our evidence portal (email addresses).
- Whether you prefer SSO (SAML) or a temporary service account + SFTP ingestion for bulk artifacts.
- Confirmation on which regional residency buckets apply for your tenants (US / EU / APAC).

To keep legal moving, can you confirm whether procurement needs a DocuSign for the privacy annex or if a signature on the master DPA will suffice? If you need a signed KMS attestation, we can provide a short attestation doc — need to know who to send to.

Attachments: privacy-provisioning-checklist.xlsx, redwood-privacy-evidence-spec.pdf

Next steps we propose:
1) HealthGrid grants two portal viewer accounts (or SSO mapping) by EOD 8/14.
2) We push a one-time inventory CSV mapping (we'll draft) and a KMS attestation stub.
3) Procurement confirms DocuSign routing or counterparty.

Happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Privacy & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the clear checklist. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- We prefer SSO (SAML) for portal access if Redwood supports SCIM user provisioning — that reduces manual overhead for our security ops.
- Procurement will likely need a DocuSign for the privacy annex addendum; Elaine is copied.
- For KMS, we need to understand the attestation scope — is it a statement of key custody boundaries (who holds the key material) or a statement of cryptographic protection in the runtime?

Two asks: could you provide a sample inventory CSV example (column headers) and a short KMS attestation stub so our security team can vet? Also include any export/control language that affects cross-border processing.

Thanks,
Tom
Director of Product Security
HealthGrid

Tom — thanks for the questions. Quick technical mapping to make vetting easier:

1) Evidence portal access
- We support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning (Okta, Azure AD). If you provide an IdP metadata URL and group mapping, we can create a read-only "Privacy Evidence Reviewers" group.
- Alternative: we can create two service account credentials and an SFTP drop that maps to the same evidence namespace.

2) Inventory CSV (sample columns)
- file_name, artifact_type (policy/diagram/attestation), produced_by, produced_at, redwood_internal_id, data_category (PII/PHI/non-PII), residency_bucket, link
- We'll attach an example CSV in the portal push.

3) KMS attestation scope
- We can provide a short signed statement that: (a) describes key custody model (Redwood-managed envelope keys + optional customer KMS integration), (b) documents that long-term key material for customer encryption is not exported outside CSR controls, and (c) lists geo-boundaries for key usage.
- The attestation is not a cryptographic certificate; it's a signed operational attestation that our security team will sign and timestamp.

4) Subprocessors & cross-border notes
- We'll include the current subprocessor CSV (names + roles) and a simple dataflow SVG that maps ingress, inference runtime (hybrid), and egress. If HealthGrid requires a tailored mapping to specific tenant routing, we can collaborate on the annotations.

I'll attach the alpha KMS attestation stub and the sample inventory CSV to this thread. Happy to join a 30m follow-up with your security ops.

—Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms-attestation-stub.txt, privacy-provisioning-checklist.xlsx
